points.name: apps.alarm.repeat.weekday_register
points.interpretation: The list-item builder registers the entry-defined weekday callback on the row and its check control using filter 7 and weekday index as user data.

points.name: apps.alarm.repeat.weekday_index
points.interpretation: The weekday callback reads its index and toggles the corresponding bit and displayed check state. Its valid domain is 0..6.

points.name: apps.alarm.repeat.event_code
points.interpretation: The weekday callback enters the toggle branch only when event code equals 7 and the index is in range.

points.name: apps.alarm.repeat.weekday_caption
points.interpretation: The list-item builder sets the localized weekday name on each created row label.

evidence: The alarm manifest registers the descriptor. Its create routine allocates state, fills seven entries with weekday labels and a common callback, publishes it as descriptor private data and constructs the list. Destroy frees descriptor private data and clears that slot; it does not clear the independent 0x20111484 alias. The builder registers the per-entry callback on both the row and its check control. The callback reads event user data and event code, checks the code and index, and toggles a weekday bit.
scope: The listed calls in the custom-repeat list builder and weekday callback while the descriptor root exists; other paths that edit or persist alarm repeat settings are not intercepted.
limitations: Indices outside 0..6 can reach an undefined-instruction trap. Altering callbacks or event values may leave the UI and saved repeat state inconsistent. Descriptor slots reduce page-lifetime exposure but are not a concurrency barrier. Shared-entry publication and rollback require system-wide quiescence. Device behavior is unverified.
